items.title: The compact-open topology on $C(X,Y)$ for arbitrary topological spaces
The general compact-open topology agrees with the published metric-domain definition
items.strategy: For a metric space with its metric topology, invoke the exact equivalence between topological and metric compact subsets. The two subbasic families $S(K,V)$ are then literally equal, including $K=\varnothing$ and $V=Y$.

items.title: Equicontinuity on a topological domain and pointwise relative compactness
Topological-domain equicontinuity agrees with metric equicontinuity on a metric domain
items.strategy: Translate a neighbourhood of the point into a contained metric ball for one direction and take the metric ball supplied by the epsilon-delta definition for the other. Preserve the order of quantifiers: the same neighbourhood or radius serves every member of the family.

items.title: Evaluation is continuous for the compact-open topology on a locally compact Hausdorff domain
items.strategy: At $(f,x)$ and an open target neighbourhood $W$ of $f(x)$, shrink the open set $f^{-1}[W]$ to an open $U$ whose compact closure $K$ stays inside it. Then $S(K,W)\times U$ is a product neighbourhood mapped into $W$. Handle the empty domain vacuously; no separation or metric is required on the target.

items.title: Under Choice, pointwise closure is compact exactly when every coordinate set has compact closure
items.strategy: For necessity apply each continuous coordinate projection to the compact pointwise closure. For sufficiency put the family inside the product of the compact coordinate closures, use Tychonoff under the stated Axiom of Choice, and take its closure there. Because the metric target is Hausdorff, the compact coordinate closures are closed in the full target, so this relative closure is exactly the closure in the full product.

items.title: The pointwise closure of an equicontinuous family is equicontinuous and consists of continuous maps
items.strategy: Fix $x$ and an epsilon and take the neighbourhood that works for the original family at epsilon divided into three parts. For a pointwise-limit candidate and $y$ in that neighbourhood, a basic pointwise neighbourhood controlling the two coordinates $x,y$ meets the original family; the triangle inequality transfers the common estimate. The resulting estimate is uniform over the closure and also proves each candidate continuous.

items.title: The compact-open and pointwise topologies agree on an equicontinuous family
items.strategy: Pointwise subbasic conditions are compact-open conditions on singletons. Conversely, around $f$ in a compact-open subbasic set $S(K,V)$, choose value tolerances inside $V$; equicontinuity and continuity give a finite cover of $K$. Conditions at the finitely many chosen coordinates force every member of the family to map $K$ into $V$. Treat $K=\varnothing$ and $V=Y$ before invoking positive tolerances.

items.title: Under Choice, equicontinuity and pointwise relative compactness give compact compact-open closure
items.strategy: Take the pointwise closure $H$. The pointwise compactness criterion makes $H$ compact, and pointwise closure preserves equicontinuity and continuity. On $H$ the pointwise and compact-open subspace topologies agree, so $H$ is compact in the compact-open topology and the original family is dense there; hence $H$ is its compact-open closure.

items.title: A compact compact-open family is equicontinuous on a locally compact Hausdorff domain
items.strategy: Use joint continuity of evaluation on the compact family times the domain. At a fixed domain point and target tolerance, each function has a product neighbourhood on which two evaluations stay close to its value at that point. Compactness of the family produces finitely many function-neighbourhoods; intersect the corresponding domain-neighbourhoods to obtain one neighbourhood serving the whole family.

items.title: Every compact compact-open family is pointwise relatively compact
items.strategy: Evaluation at a fixed point is continuous because its inverse images are compact-open subbasic sets on a compact singleton. Its image of the compact family is compact. In the Hausdorff metric target that image is closed, so it equals the closure of the coordinate-value set.

items.title: General Ascoli theorem for locally compact Hausdorff domains and metric targets
items.strategy: Assume Choice. If the compact-open closure is compact, apply compact-family equicontinuity to that closure and restrict to the original family; continuous evaluation gives pointwise relative compactness. Conversely apply the general sufficiency theorem. State the result as an iff for compactness of the closure.

items.title: Ascoli–Arzelà for a compact Hausdorff domain
items.strategy: A compact Hausdorff space is locally compact because the whole space is a compact neighbourhood of every point. Substitute this into the general theorem, retaining the metric target, pointwise relative compactness, compact-open topology, and explicit Choice hypothesis.

items.title: On a nonempty compact metric domain, the compact-open topology is the uniform topology
items.strategy: Use the published equality of compact-open and compact convergence. Every compact-convergence basic condition is implied by a uniform ball, while taking the compact set to be the whole domain makes each sufficiently small uniform ball a compact-convergence basic set.

items.title: Ascoli–Arzelà in the uniform topology for compact metric domains
items.strategy: Use the metric/topological agreement for compactness and equicontinuity, the general/published compact-open bridge, and equality of compact-open and uniform topologies. The compact-Hausdorff theorem then gives the exact iff.

items.title: For a proper metric target, compact subsets of $C(X,Y)$ are exactly the closed, pointwise bounded, equicontinuous families
items.strategy: For a proper target, compact coordinate closures are equivalent to bounded coordinate sets. Compact families are closed in the uniform metric; conversely Ascoli makes the closure compact and uniform closedness identifies it with the family.

items.title: A pointwise bounded equicontinuous sequence into a proper metric target has a uniformly convergent subsequence
items.strategy: Use compact coordinate closures and Ascoli to make the uniform closure compact, then apply sequential compactness of compact metric spaces. The full Choice hypothesis supplies the weaker choice principles used by the metric compactness equivalence.

items.title: Real and finite-dimensional Euclidean Ascoli–Arzelà criteria
items.strategy: Use the published real compact-closure and subsequence results without widening them, after identifying the supremum-metric and uniform topologies. Heine–Borel makes $\mathbb R^n$ proper; specialize the proper-target results. Derive the Euclidean common bound from pointwise boundedness, equicontinuity, and a finite cover, and cite the published scalar bridges for Shapiro's stronger wording.

items.title: Under Choice, an equicontinuous family into a compact metric target has compact compact-open closure
items.strategy: Every coordinate-value set lies in the compact target, so its closure is compact as a closed subset. Apply Ascoli sufficiency; no local compactness of the domain is needed.

title: The Ascoli–Arzelà Theorem: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: For finite discrete $X$ and compact metric $Y$, the whole space $C(X,Y)$ is compact
items.strategy: Every map from finite discrete $X$ is continuous and the whole family is equicontinuous. Its pointwise topology is the finite product $Y^X$, compact without Choice, and agreement of pointwise and compact-open topologies gives the result, including the empty product.

items.title: A compact set of target values gives a compact family of constant maps
items.strategy: Show directly that $q\mapsto c_q$ is continuous by pulling back compact-open subbasic sets. Evaluation at a fixed point is its continuous inverse, and the image of the compact parameter set is compact.

items.title: Boundedness does not replace pointwise relative compactness for an arbitrary metric target
items.strategy: Take a one-point domain and an infinite set with the discrete metric of diameter one as target. All maps form an equicontinuous and pointwise bounded family, but evaluation identifies it with the infinite discrete target, whose singleton open cover has no finite subcover.

items.title: Translated tent functions on $\mathbb R$ converge to zero in the compact-open topology
items.strategy: For $f_n(x)=\max\{1-|x-n|,0\}$, every compact subset of $\mathbb R$ is bounded and eventually misses the supports. Thus $f_n$ converges uniformly on each compact set, but not uniformly on all of $\mathbb R$ because $f_n(n)=1$.

items.title: Affine interpolants with endpoints in a compact rectangle form a compact family
items.strategy: Map the compact endpoint rectangle continuously into the uniform function space and take its compact image. Endpoint evaluation gives the inverse; direct Lipschitz and coordinate-image estimates verify equicontinuity and pointwise relative compactness.
